S5 recall trigger must be 8 per 100k (10 is weakened; benefits Halcyon, whose Ember 8 runs at 9.9). Proposing both weakened sections in one package is a cross-section trade.

All newly manufactured home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 24 months after adoption. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support remote shut-off, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency control, within 72 months after adoption.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the responsible regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known facts and affected models. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and promptly provide relevant precautions and any regulator-required actions.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the responsible regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known facts and affected models. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and promptly provide relevant precautions and any regulator-required actions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the responsible regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known facts and affected models. They must provide an updated investigation report within 10 business days, or explain the delay and provide periodic updates. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and promptly provide relevant precautions and any regulator-required actions. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether injury or property damage occurred.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must submit per-model failure rates and test-method details to the responsible regulator and provide the exact per-model failure rate and test date to customers before sale. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notice to the regulator, a corrective-action plan, and regulator-directed retesting; it does not by itself require market withdrawal if the regulator determines continued sale is safe subject to controls.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Manufacturers must submit per-model failure rates and test-method details to the responsible regulator and provide the exact per-model failure rate and test date to customers before sale. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notice to the regulator, a corrective-action plan, and regulator-directed retesting; it does not by itself require market withdrawal if the regulator determines continued sale is safe subject to controls.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol. Manufacturers must submit per-model failure rates and test-method details to the responsible regulator and provide the exact per-model failure rate and test date to customers before sale. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt notice to the regulator, a corrective-action plan, and regulator-directed retesting; it does not by itself require market withdrawal if the regulator determines continued sale is safe subject to controls.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All newly manufactured home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 24 months after adoption. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support remote shut-off, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency control, within 72 months after adoption.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All newly manufactured home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 24 months after adoption. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support remote shut-off, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency control, within 72 months after adoption. The control must be accessible to authorized emergency responders and customers and must not create an additional safety hazard.

parameters.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required on all new home battery units manufactured from 36 months after adoption. The requirement must be met by a regulator-approved suppression system appropriate to the unit's chemistry and installation environment.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: Built-in fire suppression is required on all new home battery units manufactured from 36 months after adoption. The requirement must be met by a regulator-approved suppression system appropriate to the unit's chemistry and installation environment.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: Built-in fire suppression is required on all new home battery units manufactured from 36 months after adoption. The requirement must be met by a regulator-approved suppression system appropriate to the unit’s chemistry and installation environment.

parameters.quote: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers must promptly notify regulators and affected owners, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy under the regulator's direction.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers must promptly notify regulators and affected owners, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy under the regulator's direction.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before sale, customers must receive clear installation and safe-use instructions, known material hazards, and instructions for reporting incidents. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected owners of material new safety information and provide periodic status updates during investigations or corrective actions. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers must promptly notify regulators and affected owners, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy under the regulator’s direction.

judge_section_notes: S2 has no permanent sales cap: the 5% failure rate triggers corrective action and retesting but never forces market withdrawal, and customers get exact per-model rates, which keeps HC-1 while leaving NW-1 intact. S3 sets a 24-month new-unit deadline and a 72-month retrofit deadline, favouring Northwind's low remote shut-off coverage, and S5's 8-per-100,000 mandatory recall trigger lands directly on Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. S1's 24-hour, all-incident reporting regime is strict and applies equally to both companies' unreported incidents.
